name: The Miller's Problem
description: A miller reports strange noises and a foul smell coming from his locked cellar. He believes it's rats, but hasn't gone down in three days. The rats have started fleeing upward instead of hiding, a sign something worse is below. Something old and unidentifiable has lived under the mill for years, undisturbed until now. The guild must investigate the cellar, track the smell to its source, and confront whatever is waiting beneath the mill.
title: First Real Job
epilogue: Whatever lived beneath the mill was old, territorial, and unlike anything the guild has been able to identify since. It was driven out and will not be coming back. The miller still refuses to go near the cellar, but the smell and the noises have stopped. The guild's first real job ended in a clean, if unsettling, victory.

stages.name: The Miller's Cellar
stages.flavour: The miller insists it's just rats, unusually large and loud ones. He hasn't gone down the cellar stairs in three days and has no plans to start today.

stages.name: Whatever the Rats Were Fleeing
stages.flavour: The rats are fleeing upward, into the mill and anywhere but down. Rats only run toward danger when what they left behind is worse.

stages.name: The Thing Under the Mill
stages.flavour: The creature has lived beneath this mill longer than the mill has stood. Twice it turns toward an empty corner of the cellar, as if something is there that cannot be seen.

name: The Last Clutch
description: The old hatchery at the edge of town has been failing for years. Its last keeper, too frail now to climb the coop ladder, has kept one final clutch of eggs alive through sheer stubbornness. The roof is failing and the fence is broken, and the clutch will not survive another storm without help.
title: Keeper of the Clutch
epilogue: The hatchery stands again, its old beams replaced with new timber. The keeper still visits most mornings to check the work, and so far has found nothing to complain about. The eggs are safe now, and whatever hatches from them belongs to the guild to raise.

stages.name: The Failing Coop
stages.flavour: Half the roof has already collapsed. The keeper refuses to leave the one nest she still trusts, even to eat. She does not want gold. She wants help carrying water and lumber faster than the weather can undo it.

stages.name: What the Coop Was Guarding Against
stages.flavour: Something circles the hatchery at night, testing the same weak point in the fence each time. Ordinary vermin do not show this kind of patience. Whatever it wants, it has not given up.

name: The Crow's Warning
description: Thornhollow was not burned. It was searched, room by room and drawer by drawer, as if something specific was being hunted and never found. Those bitten during the attack are slowly turning into ghouls, and no cure exists anywhere in the ruins. A crow has attached itself to the guild and refuses to leave. It may be the only reason a cure reaches Thornhollow in time.
title: Crow-Friend
epilogue: The cure held. Those bitten by the demons stayed human instead of finishing their turn into ghouls, and the tavern is full again. The crow never explained itself and never truly left either. It is still around most days, watching from somewhere just out of reach.

stages.name: Smoke Over Thornhollow
stages.flavour: The demons did not raze this town. They went through it door by door, overturning drawers and tearing up floorboards, searching for something specific and leaving everything else untouched. Raiding makes sense. This does not.

stages.name: The Trail North
stages.flavour: A crow lands on the ruined gate and does not fly off. It leads the guild north through two towns and a river crossing, toward Greywick, the nearest town with an alchemist skilled enough to have any chance at a cure.

stages.name: Greywick's Alchemist
stages.flavour: The alchemist is already grinding spider venom before the explanation finishes, her hands moving faster than her questions. Speed is the only thing that matters. The bitten are still people right now, and every hour that passes shortens how long that stays true.

stages.name: The Road Back to Thornhollow
stages.flavour: Four vials of cure, wrapped carefully and carried like something fragile and alive, are on the road back to Thornhollow. Every mile still ahead is an hour the bitten don't have to spare.

name: The Harrower's Foot
description: A second village has been culled the same way as the last one. It was not burned or looted, only searched, drawer by drawer and room by room. Whatever is directing these raids is hunting for something specific, and every emptied village brings it closer to finding it.
title: Ash-Reader
epilogue: The pattern held until the demons themselves could no longer explain it. Something, somewhere, gave every one of those orders. Nobody who fought today learned who.

stages.name: The Pattern in the Ash
stages.flavour: Every burned house in this village was searched before it burned. Floorboards were pried up and cellars emptied, nothing left to chance. This is not how raiding works. This is how searching works, and it means whatever they wanted still has not been found.

stages.name: What the Foot Soldiers Take
stages.flavour: These demons do not fight like starving animals. They fight like soldiers who know they will be questioned afterward about exactly what they found and where. Whoever gives these orders expects a full report.

name: A Demon General's Ledger
description: The foot soldiers answer to something bigger than hunger. A column of demons moves with real discipline, boots landing in step, led by something that gives orders instead of chasing its next meal.
title: Tally-Breaker
epilogue: The general kept meticulous records: names, dates, and places, tallied like a merchant's ledger rather than a monster's trophies. One word appears in the margins more than any other, written in handwriting that is not the general's own: the Harrower. Nobody at IronRest has heard the name before, but people have started asking around quietly, hoping it turns out to be nothing.

stages.name: The General's Column
stages.flavour: The demons march in formation, ranks holding even across broken ground. Demons do not normally march. Something drilled this one the way a soldier is drilled, and that is more worrying than any set of teeth.

stages.name: The Ledger
stages.flavour: Names, dates, and places. Every village it emptied is tallied like inventory, in handwriting too neat for a demon to have written. It had already left space for the guild's name before they arrived.

name: What the Culled Become
description: The Harrower's name still means nothing to anyone at IronRest, but the ledger's tally means everything. Every village it culled has since reported graves opening from the inside. The people it took did not stay taken. They came back, and they came back different.
title: Grave-Watcher
epilogue: Whatever the Harrower takes, it does not keep. It returns them as revenants, changed and obedient, still somehow counted in that ledger. East of the culled villages, in an old barrow-ground, something buried long ago has quietly begun to stir. Nobody has connected the two events yet. Somebody should, soon.

stages.name: The Empty Graves
stages.flavour: Every grave here has been dug open from beneath, dirt scattered outward in a ring. There are no tool marks and no footprints leading away, only dozens of footprints leading toward the old barrow-ground east of town, all walking in step toward the same destination.

stages.name: The Harvest
stages.flavour: They remember their own names and answer when spoken to. That is worse than if they had forgotten everything, because it means whatever they are now, they know exactly what they used to be.

stages.name: Something Older Stirs
stages.flavour: The old barrow-ground has sat quiet for three hundred years, moss grown thick over every stone marker. It is not quiet tonight. Something beneath it is moving for the first time in three centuries, and it is not moving slowly.

name: Proving the Bastion
description: The Thornhollow cure reached IronRest Bastion on schedule, carried the last leg by the guild that ran those vials there in the first place. Captain Maeryn Thorne does not forget a debt like that, and she has plenty of work that needs hands she can trust. Prove useful, and she has bigger plans in mind.
title: Lord of the Keep
epilogue: Captain Thorne kept her word, which surprised no one who had dealt with her directly. The Keep changed hands quietly, the way most important things do. The guild has had a real home since, with walls, a gate, and a garrison that answers to them.

stages.name: Officers of IronRest
stages.flavour: Captain Thorne does not say please, soften an order, or repeat herself. She has run this Bastion through worse than one guild's growing pains, and expects everyone to keep up without being told twice.

stages.name: Beasts on the Border
stages.flavour: Something is thinning the border patrols one soldier at a time. It is not raiders. Raiders do not drag their kills forty feet into the treeline and leave the boots behind, still laced.

stages.name: The Fort in the North-West
stages.flavour: Thorne's terms are simple. Take the fort back from whatever is squatting in it, and the Keep is theirs to call home, so long as IronRest can call on it when the debt comes due.

stages.name: The Demon Lord's Throne
stages.flavour: Whatever ruled this fort did not build a throne room for comfort. It built one to be seen from every angle at once, by anyone unlucky enough to be standing in it.

name: Granite Crossing
description: The Keep is finally the guild's own, and the war table already carries a new name in Thorne's own hand: Granite Crossing, home of the west coast's Stone Masons Guild. IronRest has heard nothing from it in weeks, and silence from a place that busy is never good news.
title: Garrick's End
epilogue: Garrick's raiders scattered the moment he stopped giving orders, which said everything about what kind of leader he actually was. The Stone Masons Guild has not forgotten who reopened their gate, and has made sure everyone downriver knows it too.

stages.name: The Silent Quarry
stages.flavour: Garrick and his raiders have taken the town gate and dug in as if they mean to stay a season. The stonemasons still hold everything behind it, for now, and the longer this drags on the less certain that sounds.

stages.name: Garrick's Reckoning
stages.flavour: Garrick pitched his camp inside the quarry itself, in the working pit, as if he wanted the masons to watch him do it. Stonemasons remember who does that to their livelihood, and they remember for a long time.

name: The Farm at the Edge
description: No word has come from the border farm in ten days, and now IronRest's own riders have not returned either. Whatever is out there has stopped being a farmer's problem. The Keep is sending its own this time.
title: Farmwarden
epilogue: Whatever Vayne was turning into never got to finish. The farmland recovered faster than the stories about what was found in that farmhouse basement. Most people who hear both versions decide they would rather not ask which one is true.

stages.name: No Word From the Farm
stages.flavour: The fields stand untouched, crops still ripening in neat rows. The farmhouse is another matter. Raiders have dug in around it as if they intend to winter there, not pass through.

stages.name: What Vayne Was Becoming
stages.flavour: Captain Vayne is mid-ritual when found, something dark being poured into her one measure at a time, paid for with more of herself than she has left to spend. Whatever this was meant to make her into is not finished yet. That may be the only reason there is still time to stop it.

name: The Pale Rider
description: A squire is waiting at the Keep on return, sent ahead by the Paladins of the Ashen Hand. The paladins arrive not long after, asking for help they clearly hate needing. They call the threat the Pale Rider, and by their own account, they have been losing to it.
title: Ashen-Sworn
epilogue: He dismounted, in the end. The Paladins of the Ashen Hand will not say what that looked like, and nobody who was there has pushed them to.

stages.name: The Ashen Hand's Plea
stages.flavour: These paladins do not ask for help easily. Years of training see to that. That they are asking at all, standing here in armor that has seen real use, should worry the guild more than it seems to worry them.

stages.name: The Road to Saint Aurlias Rest
stages.flavour: An old war-cleric built a church out here, long before anyone needed protecting from whatever sleeps beneath it now. Hoofprints mark this road and only this road for eleven straight miles, evenly spaced and never breaking stride.

stages.name: The Dead of Saint Aurlias
stages.flavour: These graves emptied from the inside, the same as every other place the Harrower has passed through. Here, though, the dead walk toward the church, not away from it, as if something behind that door is calling them home by name.

stages.name: The Rider in the Nave
stages.flavour: He waits behind the doors the dead were so eager to reach, seated and unmoving. He does not dismount. He has not needed to in longer than anyone currently breathing has been alive.

name: The Dragon Hunt
description: Something is burning Emberfell, northernmost of the holdfasts, one farmstead at a time. The trail leads several days north, ending in a threat larger than anything the guild has faced so far.
title: Dragonbane
epilogue: Emberfell does not burn anymore. The dragon's hoard more than covered the cost of rebuilding every farmstead it touched, which several holdfast elders have called, half joking, a strange kind of silver lining to a burned town.

stages.name: Follow the Ash Trail
stages.flavour: The ash here is cold, but the scorched ground beneath it is still warm. Whatever did this passed through recently, recently enough that it might still be close.

stages.name: Question the Survivors
stages.flavour: Every survivor tells the same story, wide-eyed with disbelief: wings spanning the width of the valley, blotting out the sky before the fire even started falling.

stages.name: Scale the Cinder Pass
stages.flavour: The only way up this mountain is the same route the dragon uses to come down. It is a narrow, ash-choked pass with no cover and no second path if something goes wrong halfway.

stages.name: The Dragon of Emberfell
stages.flavour: There is no retreat from this ledge and no fallback position. Bring everything the guild has, because everything is exactly what this fight will take.

name: Lost Kingdom Expedition
description: A kingdom that every map somehow forgot to mention has surfaced in old records. The road there is long, the ruins are older than anyone can date, and at the center of it all waits a living stone guardian nobody has gotten past yet. The patron funding the expedition is paying well enough that nobody asks too many questions about why.
title: Kingdom-Finder
epilogue: The living stone guardian went still the moment the vault finally opened, as if its only purpose had been fulfilled. The kingdom that built it remains exactly as lost as it was before anyone found this place. Some things were never meant to be found twice, and this one is going straight back to being a rumor.

stages.name: Chart the Grey Marches
stages.flavour: Six straight days of featureless grey terrain end without warning at a stone road that has no business existing this far from any charted place.

stages.name: Cross the Silent Bridge
stages.flavour: The bridge holds without so much as a creak, which is the most unsettling part of a structure that should not still be standing at all.

stages.name: Open the Sunken Vault
stages.flavour: Whatever this lost kingdom locked away down here, it locked away thoroughly. Layers of stone, then steel, then something that is neither, all sealed around a living stone guardian that has never once stopped watching the center of the vault.

name: Demon Fortress Assault
description: The guild is gathering every banner it can call on for an assault on a demon fortress. Whoever leads the breach has been asked personally, and there will be no second attempt if this one fails.
title: Hellgate Breaker
epilogue: The demon lord who held that throne will not sit on it again. The gate stands open and the wards lie broken. Whatever was singing behind them is no longer where the guild left it. It escaped in the confusion. It will not get far, but it is not here anymore either, and that is its own kind of unfinished business.

stages.name: Break the Outer Siege
stages.flavour: Ladders against the wall, fire in the ditch, and a night that refuses to end. This is the easy part, and it still costs plenty.

stages.name: Break the Warding Choir
stages.flavour: The warding choir has held unbroken for nine years, strong enough to seal a whole fortress from the inside. The goal is not to silence it for good, only to disrupt it long enough to get past the gate it guards.

stages.name: The Iron Gate
stages.flavour: Whatever holds this gate remembers the last siege in detail, and has had years to prepare for the next one.

stages.name: Descend to the Throne
stages.flavour: One door remains between the guild and whatever has been ruling behind it. It stands open already, which is worse than finding it locked.

name: Search for the Ancient Crown
description: Three crown fragments are scattered across three regions, tied together by a rumor persistent enough that half the taverns on the coast now tell their own version of it. One fragment, hidden in a fen, is said to still be guarded by a suit of ancient armor with no one inside.
title: Crownbearer
epilogue: Three fragments from three very different hiding places fit together exactly as they should. Nobody involved has explained why the crown was worth hiding in three separate corners of the world, and at this point, nobody is still asking.

stages.name: The Fragment in the Fen
stages.flavour: Cold water to the knees, colder mud underneath, and a suit of ancient armor, empty inside, still standing guard over this fragment since long before the fen had a name.

stages.name: The Fragment in the Vault
stages.flavour: The banker insists, with a completely straight face, that it is just a paperweight. That is exactly the kind of thing someone says about an object they know is worth killing over.

stages.name: The Fragment in the Fire
stages.flavour: The fragment was last seen inside an active forge, sitting in coals hot enough to melt steel.

name: The Goblin King's Warband
description: Three goblin warbands used to raid alone, tripping over each other's territory as often as they hit anything useful. Not anymore. A chieftain with more ambition than sense has welded them into one horde under a single stolen crown. They now move together, burn together, and answer to one voice. Silence that voice, and the horde should come apart again.
title: Warband-Breaker
epilogue: Three warbands, no chieftain, and a confused horde left leaderless in the hills. But the third crown pulled from the wreckage never belonged to any warlord. Whoever it actually came from has a far older claim to settle, and has not started collecting yet.

stages.name: Scatter the Outriders
stages.flavour: The outriders always give themselves away, mismatched armor clattering and torches lit hours before dark, laughing about a raid that has not happened yet. Cut them down before they reach camp, and the warband rides in blind.

stages.name: The Chieftain's Camp
stages.flavour: The chieftain holds court under three crowns stacked crooked on a head too small for any of them. They are trophies, not treasures, each looted from someone who mattered more than he ever will. He believes wearing them makes him a king. He is about to learn how wrong that is, right before the horde scatters without him.

name: The Third Crown
description: One of the goblin king's three crowns was not looted from a rival warband or plundered from a manor. It was collected as a toll on the Blackford road, taken from a lord passing through. He was reported dead that same season. He was not. Whoever he is now, he has had a long time to plan what comes next.
title: Ridge-Watcher
epilogue: The crown's true owner is not dead, not landless, and far from finished. Whatever he is quietly building at Blackford Ridge is bigger than one toll gate. Scouting it further is not the guild's job yet, but that may not last.

stages.name: The Toll That Should Not Exist
stages.flavour: A toll gate has gone up on the Blackford road again, manned by men who were farming their own fields a season ago and now answer to someone who was never a farmer.

stages.name: What the Crown Left Behind
stages.flavour: The old toll house still keeps records. One name belongs to a lord who lost everything the same season the goblin king acquired his third crown. He was reported dead. He was not, and whoever keeps these records knows it too.

stages.name: The Company He Kept
stages.flavour: Eighty men stand in real ranks, a granary stocked with grain it never grew itself, and a chain of command running two officers deep. A dispossessed lord does not build an operation like this alone, and clearly does not plan to stay dispossessed much longer.

name: The Hollow Choir
description: The guild broke a choir like this one before, at the demon fortress. They cracked its wards, cut down the demon lord keeping it caged, and left the voices behind since silencing them was never the job. It did not stay put for long. Something has settled into the old cathedral now, singing as if it means to make the place its home. It never once pauses to breathe.
title: Choir-Silencer
epilogue: The demonic choir-construct is silent this time, torn from the rafters and left in pieces on the cathedral floor. Most people have stopped flinching at an unexpected cathedral bell. Most people.

stages.name: Follow the Hymn
stages.flavour: The hymn carries for miles and never repeats a single verse. The melody is new, but the wards woven underneath it are familiar. Whatever escaped the demon fortress has made a new home in these cathedral walls. Not for much longer.

stages.name: The Choir Loft
stages.flavour: There are no singers in the loft, only a demonic choir-construct fused into the rafters in wet coils of flesh. Dozens of mouths open and close in careful sequence so the note never has to stop. It sings beautifully, which is the most disturbing part of all.

stages.name: Silence the Chord
stages.flavour: Whatever this creature has been building toward is nearly finished. Finished is not something the guild came here to allow.

name: The World-Ender's Vigil
description: Every culture that has kept records describes some version of the same ending, though never with the same name twice: something patient that waits beyond the edge of every map, not born but always waiting. Sailors marked the same blank stretch of ocean on unrelated charts a century apart, warning that the world stops arguing there. Scholars dismissed it as superstition until it appeared on land instead. It has no fixed location. It finds guilds that get close enough to matter. The guild's patron has funded five prior expeditions and none returned. He will not say what he sent them to find, only that this time he is not sending strangers. Five stages, and no easy ones.
title: World's End
epilogue: It had no name when this began, and it has none now. What it had, it no longer has. That will have to be enough of an ending.

stages.name: The Road That Should Not Exist
stages.flavour: Three nights ago, a caravan guard swore the ground opened under a full moon and a new road appeared, cutting straight into unmapped hill country. By morning, cartographers in three separate towns had drawn the same route without comparing notes, each certain they had surveyed it decades ago. The guild's advance rider stands at its entrance now, torch raised, looking down stone paved smoother and older than anyone alive could have laid it. The road did not need a ship or an army to arrive. It only needed the guild close enough to notice.

stages.name: The Watchers in the Dark Between Stars
stages.flavour: The road climbs past the treeline and past any charted sky, under stars that answer to no known constellation. Six shapes stand at the road's end, tall as siege engines and thin as famine, marking something on the empty air that leaves no visible trace. They do not turn as the guild approaches. They are not servants of the World-Ender. If anything, it answers to them. Whatever they are counting down here is only one of several debts they track, on fronts this guild has never heard of.

stages.name: The Court of the Unmade King
stages.flavour: Past the Watchers, the road becomes a hall that cannot decide on a shape, its pillars flickering between marble, bone, and nothing at all. The floor layers over itself with every battlefield it has ever hosted. On a throne built from the wreckage of every crown it has replaced sits something that at least eight vanished empires once called the first mistake. It watches the guild arrive with the boredom of something that has outlasted every guild before them.

stages.name: The Breaking of the Vigil
stages.flavour: Below the throne room, a wall of pale and thinning light holds a line that has not moved since before movement had a word for it, tended by beings too worn down to have kept their faces. Whatever has held this post can no longer pretend it does not need help. The guild braces the failing wall alongside things that stopped being anything nameable long ago. It will not be enough on its own. It has to be enough anyway.

stages.name: The World-Ender
stages.flavour: Past the breaking vigil there is no more road, no more sky, only a shape the size of a held breath, waiting exactly where it has always waited. It does not introduce itself. It has never needed to. Whatever happens next will be the last thing every one of the five prior expeditions ever saw, or the first thing one of them survived, with someone left to write down the difference.

name: The Last Pilgrimage
description: Travelers along an old, unofficial road have gone missing near a waystone shrine and returned changed. They were not robbed or killed. They were claimed, made to kneel through unknown rites they never agreed to before being released. Every map marks the shrine as abandoned, and has for longer than anyone can say. Whatever is using it now is not abandoned at all.
title: Pilgrim's Herald
epilogue: There is a name for what the guild found beneath that archive, and it is not a monster's name. It once mattered enormously to people who no longer exist to say so. It is still down there, waiting for a pilgrimage that stopped coming centuries before anyone alive could feel guilty about it.

stages.name: The Waystone
stages.flavour: What the survivors describe is not a monster in the usual sense. There are no claws, no roar, nothing that wants a fight. Only something old and confused, pressing strangers through the motions of a rite it still believes someone is meant to receive. It does not attack so much as insist. That is somehow worse.

stages.name: The Scribes' Silence
stages.flavour: An order once kept the records here, every pilgrim's name and every final rite, generation after generation, until one day nobody wrote another entry and nobody came back to ask why. The building still stands locked exactly as its last scribe left it. Whatever moves inside is not guarding treasure. It is guarding an unfinished ledger, the same way the shrine outside is still trying to finish a rite.

stages.name: What the Archive Remembers
stages.flavour: Half the pages have turned to dust, and the surviving half do not agree with each other. Names are spelled three different ways, dates contradict, and a century of scribes each half-finished what the last one started. Pieced together, the shape that emerges is not abandonment or betrayal. It is a custom that quietly stopped, one skipped generation at a time, until nobody left alive remembered why the walk had mattered.

stages.name: The Road That Still Opens
stages.flavour: Beneath the archive's last sealed room, a second road begins, the real one that the shrine outside was only ever an echo of. It leads nowhere on any chart and never was going to, but it remembers one condition for opening: someone willing to walk it in the missing pilgrims' place. The guild did not come here to volunteer for that. It seems the road does not care.

name: The Hollow King's Return
description: For guilds a run or two into prestige. The barrow-ground that has been stirring quietly for months has stopped being quiet at all. The king everyone assumed was safely buried is not staying that way, and whatever is escorting him back out is worse company than he ever was.
title: Kingslayer Twice Over
epilogue: He is buried again, properly this time, under considerably more stone than the last attempt managed. The court that followed him has not been seen since, which is either good news or exactly the kind of quiet that comes before worse news arrives.

stages.name: The Grave Reopens
stages.flavour: The seal held for three hundred years, stone unmoved and wards unbroken. It held for exactly one night less than it needed to.

stages.name: The Procession of the Dead Court
stages.flavour: Every advisor he ever had executed now walks behind him in perfect procession, and not one of them looks angry about it anymore. That is the part that should worry the guild.

stages.name: The Bridge of Forgotten Oaths
stages.flavour: This bridge bears the weight only of those who never once broke a promise in their lives. Cross carefully.

stages.name: The Second Coronation
stages.flavour: He is nearly home. The crown still remembers the shape of his head, even though the kingdom beneath it forgot his name long ago.

name: The Man Who Sells Maybe
description: A cart has been working the roads outside town for a week, selling something described only as a chance. Three separate people have already asked the guild to look into it, each for a different reason, and none of them flattering.
title: The One He Doesn't Cheat
epilogue: Grimsby never gave a straight answer about where the cart came from or where the coin under the floorboard was headed. What he did give, once he stopped talking his way out of it, was his word, worth exactly as much as anyone's word is worth once it has been checked. He still turns up unannounced and still charges for the privilege, but the deck is real now, and everyone involved knows it. That may be the most honest thing Grimsby has ever agreed to.

stages.name: A Cart That Wasn't There Yesterday
stages.flavour: The wheel ruts run in a perfect circle and go nowhere. Whoever owns this cart never actually left. A hand-lettered sign promises a fair chance for a fair price, the kind of phrase that usually means the opposite of both halves. Three townsfolk are already lined up, each certain they are about to win big.

stages.name: The Deck Has an Opinion
stages.flavour: A little patience is all it takes. The same three cards come up jackpot for the man running the table, and only for him, four times running. He is good enough that nobody else has caught it, but not good enough to fool someone actually watching for it. He notices the exact moment he is made, and does not look surprised.

stages.name: What Grimsby Actually Owes
stages.flavour: Caught cold, Grimsby neither runs nor grovels. He negotiates, as if getting caught was always step two of the plan. The real trouble is not the rigged table. It is the two far less patient men he still owes for the cart itself, and they have just watched the same show everyone else did. A fair chance was never the actual pitch. Buying enough goodwill to still be standing tomorrow is.

name: Bandits on the Old Road
description: Every caravan coming up the old trade road tells the same story: a toll demanded at knifepoint, sometimes by a different crew than the week before. There are too many bandits, too well coordinated, for this to be a handful of desperate strangers acting alone.
title: Roadwarden
epilogue: The self-styled king of the old road answered for every toll he ever collected, all at once. The road is clear again, for now. Someone always notices an unguarded stretch of road eventually, but that is a problem for whoever is watching next season.

stages.name: The Toll Nobody Asked For
stages.flavour: A merchant's convoy limps into town short two wagons and a good deal of coin, describing the same crew that has hit half a dozen others this month. They were organized, patient, and unsettlingly polite about the robbing.

stages.name: Whose Colors Are These
stages.flavour: A torn banner left at the ambush site does not match any crew the guild has dealt with before. Asking around turns up three other independent bandit gangs flying the same colors, as if someone has been recruiting rather than competing.

stages.name: The Self-Crowned King of the Old Road
stages.flavour: He has built himself a proper little court out of a collapsed watchtower, complete with a title nobody gave him and a small army of bandits who apparently had no better offer. Someone should tell him how this usually ends.

name: Something Big in the Foothills
description: Herders in the foothills keep losing whole flocks overnight to hill giants. What is left behind is not the tidy work of wolves or the opportunistic mess of bears. Fence posts are uprooted rather than chewed through, and the tracks in the mud are the wrong size and shape for any known predator.
title: Ridgebreaker
epilogue: The warband has broken up and scattered back up the ridge, minus its biggest member. The foothills will probably see another band of hill giants eventually, since they rarely get wiped out so much as get bored and move on. That is a problem for a different season.

stages.name: Torn Fences, Missing Herds
stages.flavour: The fence was not broken so much as removed, posts and all. The drag marks leading up into the hills are wide enough for two grown men to walk side by side without touching the edges.

stages.name: The Ridge Warband
stages.flavour: This is not one hungry animal passing through. It is a hill giant warband, half a dozen strong, with a crude but functional camp built from stolen timber and whatever livestock they have not already eaten.

stages.name: The Ridgebreaker
stages.flavour: The warband's biggest hill giant earned that name honestly. There is a boulder near the camp with a deliberate, deep dent in it, apparently left just to make a point to the rest of the group.

name: Full Moon Over Ashvale
description: The hunting lodge town of Ashvale wants a wolf problem solved before the next full moon. The tracks are shaped wrong, the attacks escalate on a fixed schedule, and at least one survivor has started acting like they are waiting for something.
title: Moonhunter
epilogue: The werewolf pack has gone quiet, its alpha put down before the moon finished rising. Ashvale is grateful, if rattled. One of the people the guild was sent to protect did not make it through the last stage of this the way anyone would have wanted. Nobody is saying that part out loud yet.

stages.name: Not Wolves
stages.flavour: The bite radius is wrong for a wolf, and the kills are too organized for a pack of animals. Every attack so far has landed within a day of the moon's phase, which is either an enormous coincidence or exactly what it looks like.

stages.name: The Turned Neighbor
stages.flavour: One of the survivors the guild was sent to protect stopped answering to their own name three nights ago. By the time anyone noticed, it was already too late to do anything gentle about it.

stages.name: Under a Full Moon
stages.flavour: The pack has run wild under a full sky before, and it will happen again unless the guild reaches the alpha before moonrise finishes. After that, there is no version of this fight anyone walks away from clean.

name: The Body Snatcher Problem
description: A prominent Ironrest household has started acting subtly wrong. The words are right, but the rhythm is off, and every laugh lands a half second late. Nobody can point to exactly what has changed. Everyone agrees that something has.
title: Unmasker
epilogue: The body-thief that had been wearing that household is gone now, and so is whatever it was actually made of underneath. The real question, how long it had been doing this and to how many other households nobody has checked, goes conveniently unasked by everyone who would rather not know the answer.

stages.name: Wrong Rhythm
stages.flavour: Every answer the family gives is technically correct and somehow still feels rehearsed, as if something learned the shape of a normal household by watching it rather than living in it.

stages.name: The Grave-Robbers' Trail
stages.flavour: A disturbed plot in the family crypt leads to a much larger operation than one household's worth of graves. Someone, or something, has been quietly harvesting bodies for far longer than anyone has noticed.

stages.name: What Wears Them Now
stages.flavour: It is not undead, and it is not wearing a stolen face the way a shapeshifter would. It is copying, methodically, from the inside out, and it does not want to be interrupted.

name: Hunt-a-Lich
description: Raised dead have been getting bolder and far better organized than any ordinary wight problem. Someone, or something, is directing them with real intent, and the pattern only makes sense as the early moves of a much longer game.
title: Grave-Marked
epilogue: The guild found where the lich is holed up, an old ossuary nobody has bothered mapping in decades, but not what he is actually planning underneath it. He is confident enough in it to have stopped hiding, and that confidence should worry everyone more than it currently does.

stages.name: The Dead Don't Usually Plan
stages.flavour: These are not the shambling, purposeless dead the guild has cleared out before. They take positions, fall back when overwhelmed, and regroup somewhere the guild has not found yet. Something is thinking for them.

stages.name: A Name in the Dark
stages.flavour: A captured ritual circlet, still warm, carries the same signature over and over. It is a name half-erased by time and deliberately obscured the rest of the way, belonging to someone who was supposed to have died a very long time ago.

stages.name: The Door He Didn't Bother Locking
stages.flavour: The ossuary door is not warded, guarded, or hidden. Either he does not know the guild is close, or he wants them to walk in exactly like this, on his schedule instead of theirs.

name: Quiet in Millbrook
description: Every report out of Millbrook says the same unsettling thing in a different way: the town looks fine and sounds fine, but is not. Residents show flat affect and give identical answers despite never having met, and a whole community has suddenly started agreeing on everything a little too easily.
title: Watcher of Millbrook
epilogue: Nobody in Millbrook is exactly lying. They answer every question truthfully, and every answer arrives at the same conclusion no matter what was actually asked. The guild traced the compulsion to something underneath the town before the trail went dark. Whatever it is, it noticed them looking.

stages.name: Flat Answers
stages.flavour: Every resident gives the same measured, faintly rehearsed answer to a completely different question, down to the same half second pause before speaking, as if they are all listening to something before they respond.

stages.name: The Trail Goes Quiet
stages.flavour: Whatever is directing Millbrook does not panic when it is noticed. It simply goes quieter, tightening its grip rather than loosening it, until every lead the guild had goes suddenly and deliberately cold.

name: The Loom Beneath
description: Whatever went quiet under Millbrook has not stopped. It has simply stopped being subtle about it. Tracing the compulsion to its root leads underground, to something that was never a person and has apparently been weaving many of them together for longer than anyone in Millbrook has been alive.
title: Thread-Walker
epilogue: The guild has a name for it now, the Loom, for lack of anything it has ever called itself. They have a location, and a fairly complete picture of what it has been doing to Millbrook and probably other towns nobody has checked yet. What the guild does not have is any plan that avoids someone going down there to end it directly.

stages.name: Underneath
stages.flavour: The tunnels beneath Millbrook were not dug by anything with hands. The walls are smooth in a way that looks grown rather than carved, and every thread of pale fiber running through the stone pulls faintly toward the same direction.

stages.name: One Voice, Too Many Mouths
stages.flavour: It does not attack. It talks calmly through every captured townsperson at once, in perfect unison, asking in a dozen borrowed voices why the guild would want to unravel something that finally made everyone agree.

name: The First Haul
description: A grizzled old quartermaster corners the guild before their first real job is even finished. He insists that buying every scrap of ore and timber from the shop is money any guild worth the name should be keeping for itself, if someone is willing to clear the bramble off the old gathering grounds first.
title: Provisioner
epilogue: The quartermaster has shown the guild everything they know about coaxing ore, timber, herbs, and fish out of the land around Ironrest. The rest is just standing at a node and paying attention. The supply room already looks less bare, and the shop counter is bleeding a lot less gold.

stages.name: Clearing the Old Grounds
stages.flavour: The gathering grounds have not been touched in years. Brambles cover the quarry mouth, the woodyard has not been swept, and the herb garden has gone to weed. None of it is dangerous. All of it needs clearing before anyone can use it again.

stages.name: A Lesson in the Old Ways
stages.flavour: The quartermaster walks the guild through every node personally: when to strike, when to wait, and which glints are worth rushing for. It is less a lesson than a demonstration of forty years spent never once paying for a single nail.

name: The Kindred Moon
description: A letter reaches the guild from Ashvale, addressed by name and asking, carefully, not to be read aloud to anyone else. The man who wrote it survived the pack the guild put down there -- survived the bite, too, and has spent every month since hiding what that actually means. The next full moon is close enough to count in days.
title: Kindred
epilogue: He is still standing when the moon finishes rising, which was never the safe assumption. What walked out of that circle remembers Ashvale, remembers the letter, remembers exactly who he is -- the shape changed permanently; nothing underneath it did. Ashvale does not know what to do with that, and hasn't decided whether it's grateful. The guild has already made up its mind.

stages.name: A Name From Ashvale
stages.flavour: The letter doesn't ask for a cure, not in so many words -- it asks for privacy first, help second, and mentions, almost as an afterthought, that the wound from that night never fully closed. Ashvale doesn't know. He'd like to keep it that way for as long as possible.

stages.name: What the Hedge-Witch Wants
stages.flavour: The old woman who might know a rite worth trying does not do anything for free, and what she wants this time is already dangerous before anyone factors in that she wants it fetched during the wrong week of the month. She's not unsympathetic. She's just not going to pretend this is simple.

stages.name: The Rite at Ashvale
stages.flavour: The circle only has to hold until the moon finishes rising, which is exactly the part nobody can promise. He's already changing by the time the first attempt goes wrong -- not the pack's kind of wrong, something older and less patient, drawn by the same working that's supposed to be helping him.

stages.name: What Walked Out of the Circle
stages.flavour: Something is standing where he was, and for one very long moment nobody, including him, is certain which parts of him made it through. Then he says the guild's name, correctly, and asks if it worked.
